outcomes.text: Read a wide range of fiction and non-fiction: whole books, short stories, poems and plays across genres, periods, forms and authors.
Read high-quality English literature, pre-1914 and contemporary, covering prose, poetry and drama.
Read two Shakespeare plays and seminal works of world literature.
Choose and read books independently for challenge, interest and enjoyment.
Re-read earlier books to become familiar with them and make comparisons.
Learn new vocabulary, link it to known words and work out meaning using context and dictionaries.
Make inferences and support them with evidence from the text.
Use the writing's purpose, audience and context to support comprehension.
Check understanding while reading to make sure the text makes sense.
Explain how figurative language, word choice, grammar, text structure and organisational features create meaning.
Recognise a range of poetic conventions and how they are used.
Study setting, plot and characterisation and their effects.
Explain how dramatists' work is communicated through performance and how alternative staging allows different interpretations.
Make critical comparisons across texts.
Study a range of authors, at least two in depth each year.
Write well-structured formal expository and narrative essays.
Write stories, scripts, poetry and other imaginative writing.
Write notes and polished scripts for talks and presentations.
Write other narrative and non-narrative texts, including arguments and personal and formal letters.
Summarise and organise material and support ideas and arguments with necessary factual detail.
Apply growing knowledge of vocabulary, grammar and text structure and select the appropriate form.
Use literary and rhetorical devices from reading and listening to strengthen the impact of writing.
Plan, draft, edit and proof-read, considering how writing suits its audience and purpose.
Amend vocabulary, grammar and structure to improve coherence and effectiveness.
Use accurate grammar, punctuation and spelling, applying the key stage 1 and 2 spelling patterns and rules.
Extend and apply key stage 1 and 2 grammatical knowledge to analyse more challenging texts.
Study the effectiveness and impact of grammatical features in texts they read.
Draw on new vocabulary and grammatical constructions from reading and listening and use them deliberately for effect.
Know the differences between spoken and written language, formal and informal registers, and Standard English and other varieties.
Use Standard English confidently in writing and speech.
Discuss reading, writing and speech using linguistic and literary terminology precisely.
Use Standard English confidently in formal and informal contexts, including classroom discussion.
Give short speeches and presentations that express their own ideas and stay on point.
Take part in formal debates and structured discussions, summarising or building on what others said.
Improvise, rehearse and perform scripts and poetry, using role, intonation, tone, volume, mood, silence, stillness and action.
